checks.name: function_identity
checks.rationale: Binary Ninja, Radare2 6.2.0 and angr 10.0.4.post1 CFGFast each recover exactly one function at 0x0048F0D0 spanning 10 bytes with 3 instructions, one basic block and no edges. The current translation unit defines exactly one function for this address, StoreInstanceHandle. Binary Ninja's FX_SmokeEmit_22 and Radare2's fcn.0048f0d0 are placeholder names.

checks.name: argument_mapping
checks.rationale: Retail reads its only argument from [esp+4] (the cdecl argument immediately above the return address) as a 32-bit value. main 0x0048F530 pushes EBP at 0x0048F5F9, and EBP holds WinMain's first argument (HINSTANCE) loaded at 0x0048F585 from [esp+0x478]. The candidate declares void* __cdecl(void*), consuming the same one pointer-width argument at [esp+4]; there is no second or hidden stack parameter.

checks.name: constants_and_scaling
checks.rationale: The body has no literal constants, no scaling and no arithmetic. Its only memory operands are the argument slot and the 32-bit absolute global at 0x005C8BC0 encoded in a3c08b5c00. The candidate body contains no source constant; the store address is the linker relocation of InstanceHandle.

checks.name: memory_layout_and_access
checks.rationale: Retail performs exactly one 4-byte store to 0x005C8BC0 and reads no global. The candidate performs exactly one 4-byte store of the argument to the 4-byte global InstanceHandle; the fresh -O3 object encodes the store as mov %eax,<dir32 .bss+4> (InstanceHandle, at .bss+4 after AppTitle was added at .bss+0). The current linked image f9f3b9ee... places InstanceHandle at 0x005E1BBC (nm) and the captured candidate store resolves there; the receipt 158f189c... validates against the current tree. The previous linked image 596d15c4... placed InstanceHandle at 0x005D5BB8 before AppTitle was added; that offset is historical. Access width and kind match and no other memory is touched.

checks.name: calls_and_side_effects
checks.rationale: There are no call instructions. The only side effect is the single dword write to 0x005C8BC0, after which the function returns immediately; the candidate performs that store through InstanceHandle and has no additional side effect.

checks.name: return_and_error_paths
checks.rationale: The function has exactly one basic block, no branches and no calls, so it has one return path and cannot fail. EAX is the loaded argument and is also the value stored, so the return value is the argument bit-for-bit. Radare2 ESIL executed the retail bytes for 0x00000000, 0x00000001, 0x11223344, 0xFFFFFFFF and the other differential inputs: EAX and the dword at 0x005C8BC0 both received the argument and the neighbouring words stayed 0xC3C3C3C3 in every case. The 10-case differential in scripts/native_diff_runner.py was re-run against this revision (337c5d5726e7d7ddc366dcece75a990ccdf7b7d436a8cf15a930b12e911dba3a) and the fresh -O3 object (e2dad9571a80b7071a3e179419dbf35febaf29ecc36faec0851142a12dc73883); all 10 cases matched. The only caller, main 0x0048F530, calls this at 0x0048F5FA and does not read EAX afterwards (the next instruction pushes the literal address of "filesys.cfg"), so this corrected return is contract-correct but not consumed by that caller.

checks.name: floating_point_semantics
checks.rationale: The body performs no floating-point load, store or arithmetic and reads no FPU state.

limitations: The reviewed scope is the single observed retail path; the function has no alternate or error path.

The CFG evidence recorded for this native is retail-image structure: Binary Ninja and Radare2 independently recover the same one-block graph from igi.exe. The cfg_similarity value of 1.0 is the agreement of those two retail graphs, not a candidate-versus-retail score.

Candidate structural equivalence rests on the identical one-block load/store/return shape (verified in the fresh -O3 object and the 10-case retail-vs-candidate differential in scripts/native_diff_runner.py) and on the paired typed Frida capture for one startup call: all 31 compared fields matched, including the argument class, return alias, previous-null store delta and the created-window HINSTANCE relation. That capture is single-call and single-scenario; it does not prove other paths or runtime equivalence generally.
The retail caller at 0x0048F5FA discards EAX, so the corrected return value cannot be observed in the current start-up trace even though it is part of the function contract.

The candidate stores to its own mapped InstanceHandle global rather than retail 0x005C8BC0. The current tested image f9f3b9ee... places it at 0x005E1BBC, and the manifest runtime_layout maps retail 0x005C8BC0 to the candidate InstanceHandle symbol. The historical image 596d15c4... placed it at 0x005D5BB8; that offset is not current. This review compares the single store relation, not process-wide memory-layout equivalence.

The behavioural differential executes the retail bytes in the Radare2 ESIL emulator and the candidate as a host-built translation unit; neither game process was launched. It is not a live IGI.exe observation.

Neighbouring native 0x0048F0B0 has its own record. The earlier wrong-global defect was corrected: retail 0x0048F0B0 loads 0x005C8BD4, and the candidate now reads a separate AppTitle global instead of InstanceHandle. That sibling's candidate AppTitle has no writer yet because retail 0x0048F100 (SetAppTitle) is only an unlinked GameNatives transcription; this is documented in the 0x0048F0B0 record and is not claimed here.

The candidate and 0x0048F080, 0x0048F0B0 and 0x0048F0C0 share one translation unit, so this implementation digest also binds those siblings' source; the 0x0048F0B0 correction changes the shared .bss layout but not the body reviewed here.

Runtime scope is one call per side, level 1, windowed, command line "window level1", one game-data working directory. Argument consistency is true over one observed call; the retail call site 0x0048F5FA is statically unique but a second call was not exercised.

The accepted candidate image f9f3b9ee... was rebuilt by concurrent work in the shared worktree at 2026-10-23T10:11:34Z; the task-context image 11f93920... is no longer present. Attempt 1 observed 24/24 primary fields matching on 11f93920... but lacked the candidate window relation. A later concurrent rebuild would supersede the tested image/receipt pair.

The candidate window class is "IGI.Retail.ModelScene" while retail uses "Innerloop"; class names are per-side identification and are not compared. The HINSTANCE relation is read at CreateWindowExA/W return via GWL_HINSTANCE; window visibility, style, title and class equivalence are outside scope.

The paired capture used a 30 s post-call observation bound (precedent default 5 s) to avoid the startup/window-creation race; the bound and the action probe were identical on both sides, and the observed window relations arrived at 2.405 s (retail) and 0.206 s (candidate).

Attempt 4 was disturbed by a foreign retail igi.exe launched by concurrent work in the same worktree; it was never attached to, signalled or terminated. The final preflight was clear on the decisive Frida list, and no game/probe process remained after the accepted capture.
